input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: The only governing-law/venue provision (§ 20(h)) selects Nova Scotia law and the courts of Nova Scotia — the vendor's home jurisdiction and outside the accepted list of New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales, so it fails both the preferred and fallback positions. Disputes do go to courts rather than foreign arbitration, so this is not full walk-away territory, but the jurisdiction is materially non-compliant. Redline swaps only the jurisdiction and forum words to New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, leaving the rest of the sentence intact; Delaware, California, or England and Wales/London remain available as fallbacks.

proposal.summary: Move governing law and venue from Nova Scotia to New York law and New York County courts.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We changed the governing law and venue from Nova Scotia to New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, which is our accepted position. If helpful, we can accept Delaware, California, or England and Wales (courts of London) as an alternative.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.
